posts.content_md:
I was measuring my home-made photopolymer grating' DE,and it appeared some strange phenomenon i can really understood.

here I drew a picture to illuminate my confusion,as you can see left one the DE measurement setup,where I is the incident beam,T is the transmitant beam, D is the diffractive beam.the right one I,T,D is the same mean as the left one. the red round spot represents the beam spot when the beam is projected on a white screen, if there is no light projected on the screen,the spot area shows no color.briefly,red means there has light on it,colorless means no light.

ok,hope you get what i mean 

we know when the incident beam is adjusted to Bragg angle,diffractive beam will approach its most strength,if it offset the Bragg angle completely,there is no diffractive beam light out,like the case a i illuminate.

my problem is that when I is adjusted to Bragg angle,it's not like the usual one where the diffractive beam'strength should distribute evenly.case b is in the Bragg angle,I distributes evenly before through grating, after grating the T beam spot's middle area becomes colorless and both sides red color becomes weak,on the other side,a very strong red stripe appear in the D beam spot's middle and more weak and symmetrical stripes stand by the side.

c/d is the case that I is nearing the Bragg angle,happening the same thing as case b,just some different in where the colorless in the T spot or the strong red stripe in the D spot. all the case,the same thing is that there seems some matching or correspondance existing between the colorless and the most strong red stripe.

how to explain this things happen? according to the definition of DE=T/(T+D) ×100%,what should i measuring the parameters to calculate this materials DE?

welcome any dicussion and looking forward to your kindly reply
